content.text:
Because "the compiler" only touches one of the three places that path is used. The other two are plain Node with no resolver in the loop:

| Site (`vite.config.mts`) | What sees the path | Extension probing? |
|---|---|---|
| `fs.existsSync(plugin.manifestPath)` (line 71) — the gate that decides whether an `apps/*` dir is a plugin at all | Node `fs` | No — it checks for a file literally named `manifest` |
| `isPluginManifestPath()` (line 122) — matches chokidar `add`/`unlink` events | string compare on the real on-disk filename | No — the watcher hands you `…/src/manifest.ts`, you have to know what to match |
| `import X from "/@fs/…/manifest.tsx"` (line 263) — generated virtual module | Vite's resolver (`tryFsResolve` → `resolve.extensions`) | **Yes** — this one could be extensionless |

So you could drop the extension from the import string, but you'd still need the extension list for `existsSync` and the watcher matcher — the list has to exist somewhere, and the PR just uses it in all three spots for consistency.

The "let Vite decide" version would be `await this.resolve(path.join(pluginRoot, "src", "manifest"))` inside the `load` hook — that returns `null` for missing files, so it replaces `existsSync` too. But discovery becomes async and hook-bound, and the watcher matcher still needs extensions. More churn than a two-item array.

One lazier variant if the real gripe is hardcoding `ts`/`tsx`: the file already has `LOCAL_PLUGIN_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` (line 37). `LOCAL_PLUGIN_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS.map((ext) => \`manifest${ext}\`)` reuses it and deletes the new constant — at the cost of also accepting `manifest.js`/`.mjs`, which is a design call.

Done — on `ENG-914-fix-plugin-auto-discovery`, working tree only.

`vite.config.mts:50-68` — discovery is now one `fs.globSync` over the existing `LOCAL_PLUGIN_SOURCE_EXTENSIONS` list; `LOCAL_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_FILES`, `resolveLocalPluginManifestPath`, the `existsSync(appsDir)` guard and the `flatMap` are gone. `isPluginManifestPath` (line 118) matches the same list. Docs say `manifest.*`.

Versus the PR's `+32/-8`, this is **+19/-44** overall.

Verified without node_modules (it's empty here, so no `tsc`/`vite`): a temp `apps/` fixture returns exactly the two dirs that have a manifest, correct slugs/import names/sort, `[]` for a missing root; watcher matcher accepts `…/src/manifest.{ts,tsx,js}` and rejects siblings and host `src/`. Prettier (defaults) clean. Not run: `tsc --noEmit` and an actual dev server — `npm ci` first if you want those.

→ skipped: dedupe when one app ships both `manifest.ts` and `manifest.tsx` (would emit two imports with the same name). Left a `ponytail:` comment; make it throw if it ever bites.
→ side effect: `manifest.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs` now count as manifests too. Want `.ts`/`.tsx` only, say so — it's `manifest{.ts,.tsx}` plus `/src/manifest\.tsx?$/`.
